chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Yazid ibn Mu'awiya (may Allah curse them) performed Hajj. When he returned, he recited poetry: 'When we make our right hand empty (of strength/power), we shall not return in our years for Hajj and Umrah as long as we remain.' So Allah shortened his lifespan and killed him before his appointed time.

key_terms.ثَافِلاً: Empty, void, or lacking (referring to power or life)
key_terms.لَعَنَهُمَا اللَّهُ: May Allah curse them (often used for multiple entities or emphasizing the curse)
key_terms.يَزِيدَ بْنَ مَُعَاوِيَةَ: Yazid ibn Mu'awiya, the Umayyad Caliph

ai.seo_question: What happened to Yazid ibn Mu'awiya after he performed Hajj and recited his poetry?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the divine retribution upon the Umayyad caliph Yazid ibn Mu'awiya for his arrogance during Hajj, illustrating the Shia concept of *'Ilm al-Ghayb* (knowledge of the unseen) and immediate divine justice. The Prophet’s successor, Imam Ali al-Hadi (peace be upon him), records that Yazid’s poetic declaration of finality was met with Allah shortening his lifespan, a specific punishment for his spiritual hubris. This event serves as a theological proof of the efficacy of supplication and the reality of *Qada'* (divine decree) being altered by God's will.
